# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 60 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 60 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_060_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 5, Part 6 — The Servant's Extra Work: The Holy Spirit in the Flesh

**60:1** "Lord," I said, "why did the servant do more than he was commanded? Why did he dig and clear the vineyard, when he was told only to fence it?" "Listen," he said. "The servant is the Son of God, and the additional work he did beyond the commandment is a figure of his greater work."

**60:2** "For the Son of God was not content to give the commandments alone to the people, but he himself bore their sins. This therefore is the additional work that the Son of God has done, that he bore the sins of the people and suffered on their behalf."

**60:3** "Now when he took counsel with the first-created angels regarding what reward he should give to the slave for the additional work he had done, this is the council concerning the flesh of the Son of God. For the flesh served the spirit well and purely, not being at all defiled while conducting itself on earth. Therefore the reward was given it."

**60:4** "Now the Father took counsel with the Son and with the holy angels so that this flesh, which had served the spirit blamelessly, should have a resting place and not lose the reward of its service. For every flesh that is found pure and without spot, in which the Holy Spirit has dwelt, shall receive a reward."

**60:5** "You have now the interpretation of this parable." "I have, lord," I said. "Lord," I said, "hear me for a moment more." "Speak," he said. "Lord," I said, "the flesh is fragile and imperishable." "Yes," he said. "But this corruptible does not put on incorruption unless first the holy spirit is joined to it; for a man cannot put on incorruption unless he is clothed with it. Therefore when you have clothed yourself with the holy spirit, clothe yourself also with the flesh, and the flesh will be subservient to the spirit."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the Spirit-Flesh christological reflection at the close of Similitude 5.*
